subject: Private observability forwarder: final acceptance & scrub matrix
messages:
From: Aaron Li <aaron.li@finovabank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Luke Tanner <luke.tanner@thirdbridge.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private observability - scrub rules and acceptance criteria

Hi Mina / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. We want to onboard Redwood's private forwarder into Finova's SIEM pipeline for logs and traces (logs -> Splunk HEC, traces -> OTLP collector). Security asked us to confirm the following before we proceed with an on-site acceptance run:

- Scrubbing: We attached our canonical scrub list (PII, PAN regex, account numbers, user identifiers). Need a clear mapping of what Redwood will redact vs. what will be routed with tokenization.
- Batching/latency: target upper bound < 500ms on HEC forwarding; acceptable aggregator buffer < 5s. How does the forwarder behave under spike?
- TLS / certs / key management: we require mutual TLS and HSM-backed cert rotation (30d rotation).
- Evidence: we need an itemized acceptance checklist for our auditors (sample logs, proof of scrubbing, retention policy proof).

I attached the scrub list we use and a short set of scope notes. Can you reply with an acceptance checklist and any sample config you plan to use so our infra team can validate?

SRE note: we'll provision a staging HEC endpoint (staging-hec.finova.internal) and can push a 48h traffic run when you give the go-ahead.

Thanks,
Aaron
Aaron Li
Senior Platform Security Engineer
Finova Bank

Attachment: finova-scrub-list-2029.xls
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Li <aaron.li@finovabank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private observability - scrub rules and acceptance criteria

Hi Aaron — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a proposed acceptance checklist and a sample forwarder config for staging. High level answers below; details are in the checklist and the attached YAML.

Summary (short):
- Scrubbing/tokenization: Redwood forwarder supports both redaction and reversible tokenization. By default we will apply PII redaction for PAN/SSN and tokenization for account IDs (configurable). The scrub matrix mapping is included in scrub-matrix-v1.xlsx.
- Latency & batching: default flush interval is 2s; we support low-latency mode at 200ms flush for single-tenant on-prem instances (CPU/GPU not required). Large spikes are handled by adaptive backpressure + bounded disk buffering (configurable, default 500MB).
- TLS & key management: mTLS supported (client cert + server cert). We can integrate with a customer KMS for HSM-backed key material; token rotation script available — we recommend 30-day rotation to match your policy.
- Evidence pack: we will provide sample redacted vs raw comparison (sample logs), an ingestion proof (HEC receipts with timestamps), and a signed checksum of scrubbed bundles for audit.

Canary plan we propose (to be run against staging-hec):
1) Canary 1 (1% traffic, 24h): smoke verify scrubbing & HEC receipts.
2) Canary 2 (10% traffic, 24h): verify throughput and failure modes.
3) Full run (100%, 48h): production-equivalent run.

Questions for you:
- Can you confirm expected events/sec for the 48h run and a sample of log schemas we should test against?
- Do you require tokenization keys to be rotated on your side or can Redwood manage tokenization keys under a BYOK arrangement?

Attachments: forwarder-config-sample.yaml, scrub-matrix-v1.xlsx, acceptance-checklist.pdf

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Manager, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private observability - scrub rules and acceptance criteria

Aaron / team — a few additional clarifications from infra side that we'll need to be explicit about in the acceptance checklist and config:

- Payload sizing: Splunk HEC prefers payloads <= 5MB. Our forwarder will chunk at 4MB by default. We will expose max_chunk_size in the YAML.
- Compression: gzip optional — will negotiate with your HEC.
- Retries & idempotency: forwarder uses at-least-once delivery with idempotency keys for events. We'll include event-id mapping in the evidence pack.
- Backpressure & buffering: default memory buffer + disk spill to 500MB; on persistent saturation the forwarder will return 503 to clients (we will include metrics for dropped events).
- Trace hook propagation: the forwarder preserves traceparent headers and injects a redacted span_id tag when traces cross trust boundaries. We need your OTLP collector to accept 128-bit trace IDs.

Acceptance thresholds we propose to include in the checklist (pass/fail):
- Scrub success rate: >= 99.995% (sample validated against 100k events)
- HEC latency p95: <= 450ms during 10% traffic canary
- No dropped events beyond transient ACL mismatch (documented retries)
- Evidence artifacts delivered: redaction diff, HEC receipts, rotation proof

Operational runbook items:
- Token rotation window and steps (we will run a rotation test in staging).
- Rollback plan: automatic failover to buffered disk + safe-drop after 24h if HEC unreachable, with an emergency “pause” route.

I'll add these to the checklist and version the artifacts. Marissa will own the runbook deliverable for the post-acceptance handoff.

-Kim

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few quick confirmations from Finova side: 

- We can provide a 48h 100% run after the two canaries. Expect ~4k events/sec at peak during that run; average about 1.2k eps. We'll share a 10k event sample with varied schemas this afternoon.
- HSM: Finova requires HSM-backed tokenization keys for reversible tokens; our security team will share the HSM provisioning steps (we use a cloud HSM with a BYOK flow).
- Data residency: staging and production endpoints must be in us-east-1; do you support region-local forwarding?
- Audit evidence: please include time-synced HEC receipts and the scrub diff (we need a deterministic hash per batch to cross-check).

Assuming you can support HSM BYOK and us-east-1 endpoints, we can schedule an acceptance window next week. Please confirm and we'll schedule SRE on-call.

Aaron

Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2029 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private observability - scrub rules and acceptance criteria (final checklist + next steps)

Hi Aaron — thanks for the confirmations. Quick final notes and next steps from Redwood: 

1) BYOK/HSM: we support HSM BYOK flows. Kimberly and I will coordinate a dry-run for key provisioning on Monday with your security lead.

2) Region: we can bind forwarder endpoints to us-east-1 for both staging and prod. We'll surface an endpoint URL and mTLS cert chain during the provisioning call.

3) Evidence artifacts we will deliver before canary:
   - scrub-matrix-v1.xlsx (mapping of fields -> action)
   - redaction-diff-<timestamp>.tar.gz (sample diffs with deterministic hashes)
   - hec-receipts-<timestamp>.csv (time-synced receipts for batch verification)
   - rotation-proof-log.txt (result of a rotation dry-run)

4) Runbook & rollbacks: Marissa will produce a single-page runbook for your on-call with explicit rollback commands and an emergency pause toggle. Expect v1 by Monday EOD.

5) Scheduling: propose kickoff call Monday 2029-04-15 14:00 ET. Can you confirm an SRE and security point of contact?

If that works we'll mark the acceptance window on our side and send an invite.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Manager, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference

Attachment: acceptance-checklist.pdf
